svg.title: Nested CASE
svg.desc: Seven flights go through the chapter's nested CASE. The outer CASE checks dep_delay and sends each flight to exactly one branch: f1 (dep_delay NULL) to Cancelled; f2, f3, and f4 (dep_delay > 0) to the first inner CASE; f5, f6, and f7 (dep_delay -3, -6, and 0) to the ELSE branch's inner CASE. Only that branch's inner CASE runs on a row. f2 made up time, f3 arrived late, and f4 has a NULL arr_delay, so it is Diverted. f5 arrived late, f6 was on time throughout, and f7 is Diverted. GROUP BY flight_outcome then counts the labels: Diverted 2, every other outcome 1.
svg.text: Nested CASE: the outer CASE picks a branch, then only that branch's inner CASE runs
Read from the outside in. A row is checked against the outer WHENs first; the other branch's inner CASE never sees it.
WHEN arr_delay <= 0 THEN 'Left late, made up time'
WHEN arr_delay > 0 THEN 'Left on time, arrived late'
Diverted comes from both inner CASEs.
Each level checks arr_delay IS NULL on its
own; without it, a diverted flight fails
arr_delay <= 0 and falls through to ELSE.
f7 left at dep_delay = 0. 0 > 0 is false,
so the outer CASE sends it to the ELSE
